title: Semantic search chaos probe notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, somewhat messy working note for a small, aggressive probe suite we9re calling the "Chaos Probe" for embeddings used in semantic search + clustering. Goal: surface brittle failure modes early in model onboarding (multilingual and cross-domain), make a tiny reproducible prompt/candidate set for CI and for on-call debugging, and document quick manual checks for SRE/PMs to run when a regression alert fires.

Summary of approach (high level):
- Small, targeted set (~60 queries) that stresses: near-duplicate confusion, long-context drift, short-query ambiguity, topical distribution shift, code/text mixed content, and language switching.
- Candidate doc pool sizes: local smoke (100 docs), mid (1k), and stress (10k) — construct deterministic slices from the canonical embedset so CI can run quickly but we can scale up for performance runs.
- Evaluate both retrieval metrics (MRR@10, recall@k, nDCG@10) and clustering sanity signals (cluster purity for labeled topics, silhouette for coarse groups, manual t-SNE spotchecks).

Why "Chaos Probe":
- Not a replacement for full evals; meant to trigger unusual failure modes that average metrics hide.
- Lightweight and noisy by design; useful for triage and human-in-the-loop investigations.

Dataset composition and sampling notes:
- Domains included: docs/blog, product-FAQs, code snippets (python/js), tweets/forum posts, multilingual docs (en/es/ja), and knowledge-base paragraphs.
- For multilingual checks: 20 queries distributed: 10 English, 5 Spanish (es), 5 Japanese (ja). Ensure candidate pool contains relevant-language positives and cross-language near-negatives.
- Synthetic near-duplicates: take 8 canonical docs and synthesize 3 paraphrases each (rule-based: sentence swap, synonym substitution, punctuation noise) to test embedding sensitivity to surface changes.

Probe query examples (small sample):
- EN short ambiguity: "refund policy" (expected: FAQs page > blog post)
- EN long context: "How do I migrate an existing Redis cluster to the new region with zero downtime?" (expected: operations KB > migration guide)
- ES code+text mix: "como instalar pip env var python3" (expected: Spanish install guide)
- JA polite phrasing: "イベントの参加キャンセルはどうすればよいですか" (expected: event cancellation help page)
- Code snippet as query: "def fetch_user(id): return db.query('select * from users where id=')" (expected: code examples or API docs)
- Near-duplicate pair check: doc A vs doc A paraphrased -> embedding distance should be small and rank top within candidate pool.

Metric matrix (what we record in CI):
- retrieval: recall@1, recall@5, mrr@10, ndcg@10, median_rank for positives
- clustering: cluster_purity (for labeled 8-topic partition), silhouette_coefficient (coarse group), %documents_in_top3_cluster_by_topic
- stability: pairwise_cosine_stddev for same-document paraphrase group across N runs (quantize inference nondeterminism)
- cross-lingual mapping: translation-pt (query in en, doc in es/ja) recall@k

Acceptance heuristics (quick rules):
- Smoke: recall@1 >= 0.55 on local-100 smoke set OR top-3 contains correct doc for 80% of queries.
- Regression trigger: drop of >6% absolute on mrr@10 vs baseline on mid-1k set OR cluster_purity drop >0.1.
- Flavor checks: paraphrase pair median cosine must be >0.82 and lower than median for random pairs by at least 0.12.

Failure modes we want to detect (examples from prior runs):
- Tokenization-induced cross-language false matches (esp. en tokens mixing with romaji)
- Short query bias: title-similar but low-quality pages outrank KB pages (high lexical overlap but low semantic match)
- Code vs prose mixing causing embedding collapse (code query returns many prose docs)
- Batch padding truncation: long docs getting clipped which kills nDCG on long-context queries
- Quantization sensitivity: small cosine variance but large ranking flip for tied candidates

Manual triage checklist (when alert fires):
1) Re-run smoke locally with the same model commit and seed — reproduce metric drop?
2) Inspect top-10 for three representative queries (one en-short, one long, one non-en) and save snapshots (notebook: /notebooks/chaos-probe/inspect.ipynb).
3) Plot paraphrase pair distances; if paraphrase distances > 0.4 above baseline, suspect runtime change or tokenization mismatch.
4) Run t-SNE on subset (200 points) color-by-domain and by language; look for cluster drift.
5) Check model variant routing (are we falling back to a cheaper quantized candidate?).

Quick reproducible scripts and paths (notes-to-self):
- smoke runner: scripts/eval/chaos_smoke_runner.py (args: --model-commit --pool-size 100)
- notebook for triage: notebooks/chaos-probe/inspect.ipynb
- small dataset CSVs: data/chaos_probe/local-100.csv, data/chaos_probe/mid-1k.csv, data/chaos_probe/stress-10k.csv
- to add to CI: .github/workflows/chaos_smoke.yml -> runs on nightly + on PRs to model onboarding/*

Prompt sets for human eval (short):
- Q: "Does the top result directly answer the user's question?" (yes/no/partial)
- Q: "Is the top-3 overall high-quality (relevant and specific)?" (1-5)
- Q: "If not, main failure mode?" [bad-surface-match, language-mismatch, code-confusion, truncation, other]

Calibration for multilingual raters:
- English raters should annotate es/ja candidates only for obvious false positives; for subtle cross-lingual matches send to bilingual raters (Ravi/Ava).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we standardize on cosine vs dot-product in scoring? baseline uses cosine, but some runtime paths expose dot-product. Need to lock for CI. (TODO: decision in MLENG-512)
- How often should we rotate the synthetic paraphrases? currently static, but may overfit test to paraphrase heuristics. Proposal: rotate quarterly.
- Add automated adversarial transformation (HTML-noise injection) to simulate messy scraped content.

Immediate next steps (for next week):
- Finalize the 60-query list and tag each query with expected-positive-doc-id (assign to Maya to curate).
- Add chaos_smoke.yml to PR pipeline and get an initial baseline run on current production model (EVAL-BASE-2024-02).
- Share this note with eng-serving-runtime and SRE for feedback on runtime nondeterminism checks.

Appendix: current small sample table (CSV-like pasted here for convenience):
id,lang,query,expected_doc_type,notes
q001,en,refund policy,faq,short ambiguous - expects FAQ canonical
q002,en,migrate redis zero downtime,kb,should hit migration guide. long-context
q003,es,como instalar pip env var,howto,spanish how-to
q004,ja,イベント 参加 キャンセル,help,event cancellation page
q005,en,def fetch_user(id): return db.query,code,api or code example

-- end --
